memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Abram went, as the Lord had told him; and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he set out from Harran. - Gen 12:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three simple words carry enormous weight: "So Abram went." No argument, no negotiation, no request for more details. God said go, and Abram went. This is what faith looks like when it moves from the heart to the feet.

Notice his age - seventy-five. This was no restless young man looking for adventure. Abram was well settled, at a stage when most people are winding down, not setting out. Yet when God called, he went. It is never too late to obey God. He is not finished with anyone at seventy-five, or at any age.

And remember where he was leaving from: Harran - the very place his father Terah had settled and died, stopping halfway to Canaan. Where Terah settled, Abram rose and went on. One generation's stopping place became another's starting point. You are never bound by where your family stopped.

The New Testament praises exactly this obedience: "By faith Abraham, when called to go... obeyed and went" (Heb 11:8). Faith is not merely believing God's promises are true; it is acting on them. Abram's belief had feet. Whatever God has been calling you toward, faith eventually has to move. Believing is good - but "so Abram went" is where faith becomes real.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there something God has called you to that you believe but haven't acted on?
- Do you think you're too old, or too settled, for God to use you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, give me a faith that moves, not just a faith that agrees. Whatever You are calling me to, help me rise and go, trusting You at any age and from any place.
Amen.
